concerns.text: The spec restricts the study to a single model (codegen-350M) and a single dataset subset. The Idea explicitly requires repeating the pipeline with a second model (starcoderbase-1b) to 'test generality' and isolate 'model-specific variance' (Idea: Methodology step 14). The Constitution (Principle VII) mandates this multi-model approach to validly attribute correlations to code characteristics rather than model artifacts. The spec's omission of the second model fundamentally alters the research question from 'how code characteristics drive hallucination' to 'how code characteristics drive hallucination in one specific model,' which is a scientific drift.

The spec defines the hallucination index as a weighted average of automated metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, SBERT, Entity F1) but fails to implement the mandatory validation step required by the Constitution (Principle VI) and the Idea (Methodology step 13). The Constitution requires validating these automated scores against a 'manually verified subset of at least 5% of the dataset.' The spec mentions manual verification only as a success criterion (SC-003) for 'validity' but does not include a functional requirement to perform this validation or use it to calibrate the index. Without this step, the composite index may measure lexical divergence rather than factual inconsistency, invalidating the core measurement.

The spec requires only Spearman rank-correlation tests. The Idea explicitly includes 'Fit a multiple linear regression (or generalized additive model) to assess the joint predictive power' (Idea: Methodology step 12). While Spearman tests address pairwise relationships, the regression/GAM is required to assess the 'joint predictive power' and control for confounding variables (e.g., does complexity matter if length is held constant?). Omitting this multivariate analysis drops a key component of the proposed methodology.
